titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 22/2010 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ކޯޓުތަކުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު
summary: This bill amends the Judicature Act (Act No. 22/2010) to cut the Supreme Court from 7 judges (the Chief Justice plus 6) to 5, including the Chief Justice, and requires the total number of Supreme Court judges to always be an odd number. To get there, the Judicial Service Commission (JSC) would send the Majlis the names of judges it finds unfit for the post, and a judge is removed if two-thirds of the members present and voting agree. The JSC must send the names within 5 days of the law taking effect, and the Majlis must decide within 7 days after that. Both bodies may set aside their usual procedures and time limits to meet these deadlines, and removed judges keep the special benefits set out in the Judges Act.
whyItMatters: It would shrink the country's highest court and set a fast, fixed-deadline process for Parliament to remove sitting Supreme Court judges, changing who decides the final appeals in the Maldives.
keyProvisions: Article 5(a) as rewritten: the Supreme Court is made up of 5 judges including the Chief Justice, and the total number of its judges must be an odd number.
Article 5(b): for this purpose, a Supreme Court judge can be removed only if the JSC finds the judge unfit, refers the judge to the Majlis, and two-thirds of members present and voting approve.

Article 5(c) and (d): the JSC must submit the names within 5 days of the law taking effect, the Majlis must decide within 7 days of receiving them, and state bodies must complete any arrangements needed because of the removals within 7 days of the Majlis decision.

Article 5(e) and (f): judges not removed stay in their posts, the deadlines count holidays, and the JSC and the Majlis may depart from procedures and time limits in other laws and their own rules to meet them.
Article 5(g): removed judges receive the special benefits and privileges in Article 26(b) and (c) of the Judges Act (Act No. 13/2010), as decided by the JSC, paid by the state.
Clause 2: the law takes effect once it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Supreme Court judges, the Judicial Service Commission, members of the People's Majlis and anyone whose case reaches the Supreme Court.
statedReasons: The sponsor says the change is needed so that the Supreme Court is constituted under the Judicature Act the way it was before, linking this to the public's hopes for the Constitution and better conditions for citizens.
